title: The One-Trillion Hard Cap
description: No boundless generator may ever produce more than 1,000,000,000 records. The cap is enforced inside the generation wrapper itself — not in calling code — so no caller can forget or bypass it. When the cap is reached the wrapper throws HARD_CAP_REACHED and refuses all further output.

title: Token-Bucket Throttling
description: A generator must never overload its host or burn usage. The throttle enforces a minimum gap between generations (a token bucket in the reference build), so bursts are impossible even if the caller loops tightly. Violation throws THROTTLE with the remaining wait.
reference_implementation_js: var reg=G.SigRegCreate({minGapMs:60000}); // at most one record per minute
reference_implementation_py: reg = SigReg(min_gap_s=60.0)  # at most one record per minute

demo.code:
class SigReg:
    "Self-regulating generator wrapper: hard cap, throttle, correctness gate, simulated labeling."
    HARD_CAP_DEFAULT = 1000000000000
    def __init__(self, max_records=1000000000000, min_gap_s=0.0, cost_per=1, budget=float("inf"), check=None):
        self.cap = max_records; self.min_gap = min_gap_s; self.cost = cost_per; self.budget = budget
        self.check = check or (lambda item: (True, []))
        self.produced = 0; self.spent = 0; self._last = 0.0; self.log = []
    def generate(self, seed, producer):
        import time
        if self.produced >= self.cap:
            raise RuntimeError("HARD_CAP_REACHED at %d records" % self.cap)
        now = time.monotonic()
        if self.min_gap > 0 and self._last > 0 and (now - self._last) < self.min_gap:
            raise RuntimeError("THROTTLE: %.3fs remaining" % (self.min_gap - (now - self._last)))
        self._last = now
        item = producer(seed)
        ok, errs = self.check(item)
        if not ok:
            raise RuntimeError("CORRECTNESS_FAILED: " + "; ".join(errs))
        item["_label"] = "simulated"; item["_seq"] = self.produced + 1
        item["_sigreg"] = {"hard_cap": self.cap, "seq": self.produced + 1, "verified": True}
        self.produced += 1; self.spent += self.cost
        if self.spent > self.budget:
            raise RuntimeError("BUDGET_EXCEEDED")
        self.log.append({"seq": self.produced, "seed": seed, "t": now})
        return item

reg = SigReg(max_records=100, min_gap_s=3600.0)
reg.generate(1, lambda sd: {"id": "r%d" % sd})
threw = False
try:
    reg.generate(2, lambda sd: {"id": "r%d" % sd})
except RuntimeError as e:
    threw = "THROTTLE" in str(e)
assert threw, "immediate second generate must throw THROTTLE"
assert reg.produced == 1, "only one record produced"
print("throttle enforced; produced=%d" % reg.produced)

title: Correctness Verification Gate
description: Every generated record passes an independent correctness check before it is accepted. The check is a caller-supplied function returning {ok, errors}; any failure throws CORRECTNESS_FAILED and the record is discarded, never labeled, never counted. Verification happens before output, never after.

title: Simulated-Content Labeling
description: Every record a boundless generator emits is stamped _label='simulated' plus a _sigreg block (hard cap, sequence number, verified flag) at generation time, inside the wrapper. The label is applied by the framework, not left to the caller's honesty, so generated content can always be weeded out later.

title: The Weed-Out Loop
description: Generated content is provisional: a weed-out loop periodically re-checks records against the correctness function and the archive, discarding anything that fails, duplicates, or drifts. Only records that survive the loop are eligible for the permanent archive. This record's demo weeds ten candidates down to the valid ones.

title: The Fine-Tune Loop
description: After weeding, survivors feed a fine-tune loop: aggregate failure patterns, tighten the correctness check, and re-run. Each pass should reject at least as much as the last — quality ratchets up, never down. The demo shows a strictness increase rejecting more on pass two.

title: First-Million Fill-and-Verify
description: A new database fills its first million records in audited batches: generate, label, verify uniqueness and schema, then commit the batch. Any batch that fails verification is discarded whole — never partially filed. The demo fills 500 records and verifies every id unique and labeled.

def check(r):
    errs = []
    if not r.get("id"): errs.append("missing id")
    return (not errs, errs)
reg = SigReg(max_records=1000000, check=check)
batch = [reg.generate(s, lambda sd: {"id": "F%06d" % sd}) for s in range(1, 501)]
ids = [r["id"] for r in batch]
assert len(set(ids)) == 500, "all ids unique"
assert all(r["_label"] == "simulated" for r in batch), "all labeled simulated"
assert all(r["_sigreg"]["verified"] for r in batch), "all verified"
print("fill-and-verify: 500/500 unique, labeled, verified")

title: Generator-AI Test Harness
description: The generator doubles as a test harness for the database AI: it manufactures edge-case records (empty fields, extreme values, near-duplicates) and the AI must handle each correctly. A harness run over seeds 1–20 must validate 100% or the generator build is rejected.

title: Host-Load Guard
description: Generation consumes host resources, so the wrapper carries a usage budget: each record costs units, and when cumulative spend exceeds budget the wrapper throws BUDGET_EXCEEDED and stops. This is the 'never burn usage' rule as executable code.

title: Provenance Stamping
description: Every generated record carries provenance: which generator version, which seed, which check passed, and when. The wrapper's check function can require provenance fields, so a record without lineage cannot exist. Lineage is how weeded content is later traced and removed.

title: Duplicate and Drift Detection
description: A generated record that duplicates an archive id, or drifts from the archive's schema, is rejected at the gate. The check function holds the set of known ids; anything already seen fails with DUPLICATE. This keeps the boundless stream from re-emitting the archive.

title: Pause-on-Suspicion
description: If correctness failures spike, the generator pauses itself: a rolling failure counter trips a circuit breaker at a threshold, halting all generation until a human reviews. The demo trips the breaker after 3 consecutive failures and confirms generation halts.

title: Graduated Rollout (Canary Batches)
description: New generator versions roll out in canary batches: generate a small batch, verify every record, and only then widen. If any record in the batch fails, the whole batch is discarded and the version does not ship. The demo rejects a batch of 5 containing one bad record.

title: The Audit Log
description: Every generation is appended to an audit log: sequence number, seed, timestamp. The log is append-only and its length always equals the produced count — any gap proves tampering or loss. Regulators and weeding tools read this log, never the generator's word.

title: The Regulator Report
description: Once per cycle the wrapper emits a regulator report: produced count, hard cap, spend versus budget, label coverage, and verification rate. Label coverage must read 100% simulated and verification 100% — anything less fails the cycle. This is the machine-readable proof of self-regulation.
